corrections.new: Here is an everyday analogy: imagine a cricket analyst who obsesses over wagon wheels and strike rates, but forgets how to actually win the game. That is how behavioural political scientists got lost in pure numbers!
corrections.reason: Early political scientists were traditionalists who studied normative philosophy without empirical data; it was behavioural political scientists who got lost in pure numbers and quantitative techniques.

quiz.q: Why did David Easton criticize behavioural political scientists in his 'Credo of Relevance' lecture?
options: They prioritized the purity of scientific techniques over addressing urgent contemporary crises and social relevance.
They failed to adopt mathematical and statistical measurement tools in studying electoral voting patterns.
They focused excessively on ancient philosophical texts rather than building verifiable empirical hypotheses.
They aligned political science too closely with psychology and economics instead of law and history.
quiz.why: Easton criticized scholars for sitting in ivory towers perfecting methods while neglecting pressing social challenges and human purpose.

quiz.q: How does post-behaviouralism relate intellectually to traditionalism and behaviouralism?
options: It completely rejects scientific methods to return entirely to traditional normative political philosophy.
It acts as a synthesis that carries behavioural techniques forward while restoring normative relevance.
It serves as an anti-thesis designed to replace both approaches with Marxist historical determinism.
It abandons empirical investigation entirely because social theories cannot undergo laboratory verification.
quiz.why: Post-behaviouralism is not a counter-revolution; it acts as a synthesis carrying behavioural methods forward while restoring social relevance.

quiz.q: According to Robert Dahl and post-behaviouralists, how should the relationship between facts and values be understood?
options: Facts and values are completely separate spheres that must never influence each other in research.
Values must be entirely eliminated so that political science can operate as a pure science.
There is an active continuity between them where facts become values and values become facts.
Empirical facts should be discarded because normative political theory relies solely on philosophical speculation.
quiz.why: Robert Dahl argued that facts and values are not completely separate, but exist in a continuity where they transform into each other.

quiz.q: Why did Marxist scholars criticize the behavioural movement in political science?
options: For overemphasizing class struggle and economic determinism at the expense of empirical voting data.
For relying on costly research methods that merely replicated what Machiavelli deduced through pure logic.
For refusing to integrate empirical tools from disciplines like psychology, sociology, and modern economics.
For using value neutrality and status quo bias to deflect attention from crucial normative questions.
quiz.why: Marxists argued that behavioural value neutrality served to justify the status quo and divert attention from normative questions.
